title: Carbocation stability
caption: Alkyl groups push electron density towards a positive carbon (a positive inductive effect), spreading its charge. So the more alkyl groups on C⁺, the more stable it is: tertiary > secondary > primary > methyl. This decides Markovnikov products and SN1 rates.
alt: Four carbocations in order of increasing stability: methyl, ethyl (primary), propan-2-yl (secondary), 2-methylpropan-2-yl (tertiary).
description: Methyl, CH₃⁺: no alkyl groups, least stable.
Tertiary: three alkyl groups, most stable.
